dossier.public_summary: The 792 ppm ~13.3-day diplooks like a flat ~2.4 Earth-radius transit, but its depth jumps by a factor of ten from sector to sector and from transit to transit, and the signal is almost entirely made by two deep and two shallow outliers. Its period is twice the star's 6.7-day spot period, and a close neighbour can make the dip with a <25% eclipse while difference images are inconclusive. Together this favours a blended or variable-noise origin over a planet on the target.

reasons.why: Depth changes dramatically between sectors (183 ppm in sector 6, 1019 ppm in sector 33, 1690 ppm in sector 87) with chi2 112 for 2 dof and 156.3% change. sector_depths_by_source finds changes_within_a_source, so the variation is not a pipeline calibration offset, inconsistent with a planet on the target whose depth should be steady.

Individual transits are inconsistent (chi2 131.06, 4 dof), driven by two deep outliers in sectors 87 (1710 ppm and 1663 ppm) and two shallow outliers in sector 6 (165 ppm and 201 ppm). Top 3 transits dominate the signal, indicating a few bad events rather than a repeating planet.

There is a star within 1 TESS pixel that can produce the 792 ppm dip with a <25% eclipse, and difference imaging cannot place the dip on target, leaving a blended or off-target eclipsing binary as positively viable. Flat shape alone does not rule this out.

reasons.why: Period is essentially twice the stellar rotation period, and sector 6 shows large spot variability (amplitude ~1014 ppm, false_alarm ~2.706e-42) together with sectors.p_constant and transit_depths outliers. Combined with significant phase_curve amplitude 45.26 ppm (ratio_to_depth 0.05712) this supports spots/variability/blend origins over a planet, despite odd_even diff_sigma 0.528, secondary snr 1.877 and duration ratio 0.8056 having no positive binary signatures.

reasons.why: Independent scorer rates the signal well below the median known planet (0.5), consistent with the low S/N (15), extreme depth instability and centroid inconclusive, arguing against gate2 despite the 2.414 Rearth size and flat V-shape.
